accuracy.evidence: Sizes checked against the Natural History Museum Dino Directory and its size articles on 22 Nov 2026: Compsognathus 0.7 m long and 3 kg; Tyrannosaurus 12 m long, 3.5-4 m at the hips, 5-7 t; Diplodocus 24-26 m long and about 15 t; Velociraptor about 1.5-2 m long, 0.5 m at the hips, about 15 kg, 'turkey-sized' (NHM, Live Science); the Berlin Brachiosaurus (Giraffatitan) mount is 13.27 m tall and about 22 m long (Museum fuer Naturkunde, Guinness). The lab rounds to 'about' values: T. rex 7 t > one 6 t elephant and < two; Diplodocus 15 t > two and < three; Brachiosaurus 22 m = about 2 buses of 11 m; Triceratops 9 m < 11 m. Every lesson sentence uses 'about' because size estimates vary between fossils, as the NHM notes.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common beliefs about dinosaur size reported in museum education material: every dinosaur was huge (road predict, Compsognathus and Triceratops shorter than the bus, m1, challenge 'allbig'), book pictures show real size (book cards drawn the same size then put on the road, p5, challenge 'book'), longest means tallest (tall predict, Diplodocus vs Brachiosaurus questions, p4, m7, challenge 'longtall'), film raptors are real size (film predict, dashed film raptor beside the real one, m2, m5, challenge 'film'), and mixing up longer, taller and heavier (size-word gaps with per-option feedback, m6, challenge 'word').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdinosize is about comparing real dinosaur sizes with familiar things: book cards of equal size become true-scale animals on a road beside an 11 m bus, two sauropods are measured for both length and height beside a 4-floor block, a real Velociraptor and Compsognathus are set beside people and animals at one scale with a dashed film raptor, and a see-saw is loaded with 6 t elephants until it flips. It differs from flagtrack (trackways), flagdung (coprolites) and the scale labs for the Solar System (flagsolscale) in topic and mechanism; the lab_distinct gate measures it under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees each idea before the text states it: the same-size book cards turn into a tiny Compsognathus and a Diplodocus longer than two buses on the road, with a dashed line at the end of the bus to judge by; the measuring tapes show 26 m vs 22 m long and 5 m vs 12 m tall; the turkey stands next to the real raptor while the film raptor towers over it; the see-saw only flips at 2 elephants for T. rex and 3 for Diplodocus. Done messages give the rule after each task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Yes, they were all huge' (Compsognathus and Triceratops come out shorter than the bus), 'Yes, longest means tallest' (the tapes show Brachiosaurus is taller), and 'Yes, films show real size' (the real Velociraptor is closest to a turkey, the film one to a grown-up).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its slip and a message naming it: allbig ('Compsognathus was about the size of a chicken'), book ('Pictures in books are drawn to fit the page'), longtall, film and word ('heavier for weight, longer for length, taller for height'). In the lab each wrong pick also gets its own reason: the dashed bus-end line on the road, the long and tall tape values, 'That is the film raptor... came up to a grown-up's knee', and 'Not "shorter than". Diplodocus was more than 2 buses long.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with familiar comparisons (chicken, turkey, bus, house) and only the size words being taught; dinosaur names are the only long words. The adult text gives the rounded figures with 'about' and names the mistakes; validate_lessons readability passes for both. Canvas banners stay short, e.g. 'Which dinosaur is taller?'

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence gives a size, a comparison or a rule (books are not real size, long is not tall); adult paragraphs give key words, the sourced figures and why they are estimates, the common mistakes, and what each lab scene does. The content gate finds no filler phrases.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every scene before and during Show me, and 1200 px desktop: the road keeps Diplodocus (26 m) and the bus on screen with labels right-aligned, the tall scene's height labels flip to the left near the edge, the film scene names are clamped so 'Compsognathus' is not cut off, the see-saw elephants stay on the plank, and answer chips shrink their text to fit. Every action has a large button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Put them on the road, Longer / Shorter than the bus, Measure Brachiosaurus / Diplodocus, the two answer names, Grown-up / Child / Turkey and Horse / Cat / Chicken ('Closest in size: ...'), Add an elephant and Take an elephant off, and the size-word chips. The canvas aria-label follows each message with the sizes in words, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes.
